answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk: contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with zero buffer, so a lapse or cutover miss is a line-down event. That rules out defer_decision and makes switch_primary_vendor and a failed negotiate_terms unacceptable on TCO once disruption is counted, even though finance wants 18% and the incumbent has already refused a mid-cycle reopen. c1 is the matching pattern for keeping integration and deliveries intact; c6 is the only inherited cost lever that does not require changing the primary. c2 (sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboard) is the load-bearing counter-memory and is the one record worth pulling to test whether last year’s onboarding actually fits a 14-day, no-buffer window—until that original record is seen, treat “quick” as unverified for these constraints. Dual-source (c3) does not replace the expiring primary in a one-decision cycle. Uncertainty remains on whether multi-year volume pricing can approach the 18% mandate.
